Chickens can be killed at Fred the Farmer's farm, just north of the Lumbridge Market and its bank chest. It's important to use area loot for this method. Chickens drop raw chicken, feathers, and bones. The bones should be bound to your action bar to quickly bury it for prayer experience. The other items should be banked and then sold. There are also 3 egg spawns in the area, and chickens can lay eggs, which can be sold on the Grand Exchange for 336 coins, and raw chicken can be sold for 1864 coins. Feathers are dropped in quantities of 5 or 15 at a time and sells for 12 gp each.

As chickens have very few life points, a fast hitting weapon such as a scimitar is recommended for melee. For magic it's recommended to use a staff of air for an unlimited supply of air runes; abilities like Dragon Breath allow you to kill several chickens at once. One run could be completed in a minute with intense focus. There are 8 chicken spawns in the coop; if you kill all of them fast enough you have a few seconds before you can kill the second wave, after which you should have enough eggs and raw chicken to bank (the ratio may vary, this assumes 12 eggs to 15 raw chickens).

Close the door to Fred's house to prevent chickens from wandering in, making it harder to kill them and collect drops (being inside also causes you to pick up unwanted shears by area loot). Consider closing the gate as well when you are leaving for the bank to prevent them from wandering outside. All the chickens always respawn in the coop area.

If this spot is busy, there are other chicken coops on the road to Varrock, and in the farm just south of Falador.

Corrupted scarabs are a slayer monster that can be found within the Sophanem Slayer Dungeon. This method can often be used as a fully AFK money making method, however more input may be required with lower-tiered equipment. Augmented equipment with the Enhanced devoted, Biting, and Impatient perks will often give you the ability to extend your stay. You should be using Protect or Deflect from melee to survive.

Vital spark drop enhancers are highly recommended here as they will double the amount of Vital sparks received.

Lastly, to increase the amount of vital sparks dropped even further, the loot chest in the dungeon may be filled up with 30 different drops from the creatures in the dungeon. As long as the chest is full and Vital sparks are not in it, they will drop to the ground giving them a 20% chance to be doubled.

Level 1 cows in Taverley have 25 life points and always drop raw beef, cowhide, and bones. The pen can be reached by teleporting to the Taverley lodestone and running north.

  1. Start killing the cows - they have a very fast respawn time
  2. Kill 9 cows before using area loot to pick up all items
  3. Run north to the gnome banker in Burthorpe, bank the items
  4. Run south back to the cow pen, and repeat.

This area is popular with new players and competition can reduce efficiency. Try hopping worlds or alternatively there is a large cow field next to the Crafting Guild, with a bank chest at the Clan Camp.

You can choose to bury the bones instead for Prayer experience. The profit is similar (as you can carry more raw beef and cowhide which are more valuable) but is slightly more click intensive.

Level 2 cows in Burthorpe have 25 life points and always drop cowhide. The pen is located south of the Burthorpe lodestone. Start killing the cows - they will respawn instantly. Since they have a fairly long death animation, begin by killing multiple cows before looting the first cow's hide. This is faster than waiting for the first one to finish dying. Once you have 28 cowhides, click on Tanya Hyde, who is inside the pen. She will tan the hides into hard leather for 3 coins each, or soft leather, whichever is cheaper. Run north to the Bank Gnome, bank the leather, run back to the cow pen, and repeat.

For players who intend to use either Magic or Ranged, it is highly recommended to equip a weapon with decent accuracy and does not use ammunition (E.g. Mindspike, Chargebow, Quickbow). Players with sufficient Magic or Ranged levels may use Dragon Breath (5 Magic), (Chain (45 Magic), or Ricochet (45 Ranged) in order to kill more cows.

At times it may be better to make soft leather instead - hard leather is currently worth 843 gp, while soft leather is currently worth 955 gp.

out.nt: Value assumes [[Tarddian crystal]]s are made into [[crystal gloves]]. Check [[Tarddian crystal]] for optimal use.

m.h:
This guide uses an estimate of 400 kills per hour. It's possible to exceed these numbers with good equipment, but this number falls drastically as equipment worsens. While tier 90+ weaponry, attuned crystal armour, Malevolence and Greater Fury are not all required, players missing several of them may find themselves unable to safely fight more than three or four shapeshifters at once, which significantly reduces kill speeds and thus revenue.

Crystal shapeshifters drop significant amounts of rune salvage and their guaranteed drop of Tarddian crystals are also worth a decent bit of money, and under the right circumstances they can be killed very quickly.

When placed in the rooms in the Sunken Pyramid, crystal shapeshifters will always spawn in their melee form. They can change form, but they will usually only change to the form you are the weakest to, unless you're using protection prayers to defend against that style. By wearing crystal armour, which is hybrid armour (as well as providing some useful effects when fighting the shapeshifters) along with a single piece of mid-level ranged equipment you can ensure they will not change from their melee form without penalising your accuracy too much and allowing access to invention perks such as Scavenging, Biting, or Crackling. This not only means they will walk up to you so you can reach them without having to move, but also makes them use their special attack less frequently, reducing the damage taken and the risk of dying. Depending on the equipment used in other equipment slots, you may need to use higher tier ranged armour to make sure your melee defence is your lowest defence.

The crystal armour also provides a boost to damage dealt to the shapeshifters, increases the number of tarddian crystals dropped, and if at least four pieces are worn provides a chance of temporarily becoming immune to stuns, as well as clearing damage over time effects inflicted by the shapeshifters.

As the shapeshifters should be kept in their melee form at all times, and as Deflect Melee would cause them to change to a different form, and because shapeshifters consistently disable protection prayers, Soul Split is the only overhead prayer that should be used.

You may want to bring some food and a prayer potion in case of emergency, although they should usually be unnecessary. Players who struggle to keep themselves alive without it may want to bring the enhanced excalibur.

A good revolution bar for multitarget damage and healing can be found here and looks as follows: 1 2 3 4 5 6 7 8 9 0        

  • Omit Chaos Roar if not owned.
  • Replace Greater Fury with Fury if the greater version is not yet unlocked.

It is possible that you end up dying if you get repeatedly stunned at bad times, although this is relatively rare, and the reclaim costs are relatively low thanks to the low value of crystal armour.

Use area loot to easily pick up all drops. To avoid missing items that de-spawn, you will want to do this at least every 90 seconds.

Aggression potions are not required, as shapeshifters will remain aggressive indefinitely. Aggression must be toggled on by talking to Angof - this applies both to the sunken pyramid and to Tarddiad. In a small room, it is possible to have all five shapeshifters attack from their spawn points while you stand in a corner, thus maximizing the targets that Adaptive Strike will hit with its Aoe cone effect. In a large room, this is not possible due to the aggression range. You may find that, in order to aggro all of the shapeshifters, at least one of them will attack from a third direction, reducing the effect. For this reason, fighting shapeshifters in a small room is advised.

A strategy guide for crystal shapeshifters can be found here.

Dark beasts are aggressive towards all players regardless of combat level. They are known in game for dropping lots of coins as well as large and medium plated rune salvage. Players with a bonecrusher and a demon horn necklace or split dragontooth necklace can take advantage of their big bone drops to restore prayer points while Soul Split is activated. Soul Split can completely remove the need for food at high levels with high tier gear, alongside the Enhanced Excalibur.

Ranged is arguably more efficient than melee at edimmu due to the 100% hitchance on elite edimmu; however, melee is much easier due to being able to use the scrimshaw of vampyrism to assist with healing.

Activate Protect from Magic/Deflect Magic and Anguish. Place your cannon two tiles directly north of the southern pillar. All abilities are AOE using mechanised chinchompas, so just use a normal DPS rotation, prioritise Devotion so as to significantly reduce incoming damage when edimmu are grouped up.

In order to group up the edimmu, the cannon will tag them making them walk towards you, by going out of the barrier they are forced to walk into the entrance way. You cannot stay outside the barrier for too long, as edimmu have a very short aggression period if they cannot attack you, and after 6 seconds they will walk away until either you or your cannon tags them again. The aggression ability can be used to speed up kills by grouping more easily. You will run to the far end of the arena, activate aggression, then run back to the barrier.

Magic notepaper should be used to note tortured ashes, as they can be highly profitable. A pack yak can be used to send crystal seeds, weapons and shields to the bank, saving inventory space.

m.h:
This guide is written assuming 230 kills per hour with level 85 Smithing.

Chitin scraps can be used to repair the tier-90 drygore weapons. They are created by using damaged chitin on an anvil, and the amount of scraps received from each chitin scales with your Smithing level, up to 40 at level 99. Damaged chitin are received as a 100% drop from all exiled kalphite, of which the paragon is easiest to kill en masse. They are weak to arrows but are taken down just as easily with Magic. When killing kalphites, focus on one at a time using multi-target abilities when available. The kalphite paragons do not do a great deal of damage; however, this damage adds up. It is advisable to use Soul Split to help offset this damage. Quickly pick up the damaged chitin and store them in your familiar. When both yours and your familiar's inventories are full, teleport to a location with an anvil (such as Varrock, where an anvil lies near the teleport locations just south of the west bank) and use the damaged chitin on the anvil; empty your familiar's inventory and repeat. When finished, use the Bandit Camp lodestone teleport then run south to the hive. Another alternative is to use magic note paper to note the chitin as you collect them. Due to the reduced time banking there is little impact on profit but an increase in kills, experience and charm collection.

The optimal spot for killing kalphites is in the room next to the entrance to the Kalphite King's room. Getting to there from the lodestone takes approximately 60 seconds. The kalphite paragons take around 10 seconds to kill, meaning you can get 50 kills in 10 minutes when you include some time to pick up the drops. It takes less than 20 seconds to get to an anvil; from there, it takes about 60 seconds to smith all the chitin into scraps. This results in an average of 13 minute trips for 50 kills, or about 4.6 trips an hour, giving a total of 230 kills an hour.

m.h:
Fiyr Shades can be found at the end of the Shade Catacombs underneath Mort'ton. Accessing them requires a silver shade key, which is most easily obtained by burning Fiyr remains on the pyres to the southern part of Mort'ton (requiring 80 Firemaking and at least magic pyre logs), or burning Asyn remains, requiring 63 Firemaking and at least eucalyptus pyre logs. Use that key to enter the catacombs, going through the bronze, steel and silver doors.

There are four Fiyr Shades outside the rooms, and a few more inside them. You will be killing the four outside, and the room with two. Using your combat gear and abilities, quickly take down the shades. This should not be difficult as they have low defence and only 7000 LP. They will hardly hit you at all if you use ranged or magic as they only attack with melee. Wait for them to spawn, and repeat. On a highly populated world, this cycle could take less than 30 seconds. The remains are stackable in the inventory. They drop congealed blood occasionally. The shades are aggressive, so it's wise to have auto-retaliate on. No food is needed, adrenaline, and an elite enhanced excalibur should be more than enough.

After you've gathered enough remains, sell them on the Grand Exchange. They shouldn't take too long to sell because they are used in invention and gold key chances. They offer pious components with a very low junk chance. Along with tortured souls, dropped by Edimmu, these remains are the only way to get gold keys, for gold chests. Gold chests are the only chests which can contain necromancer kits and shade skulls.

The profit rate assumes 400 kills per hour using the upgraded bonecrusher. Your actual profit may be higher or lower depending on your speed.

Frost dragons are commonly killed for their 100% drop of frost dragon bones, worth 14,871 gp each. Combining the Death Note relic, which requires level 108 Archaeology, with the upgraded bonecrusher allows bones to be automatically noted and picked up, increasing profits significantly. Alternatively magic notepaper could be used, but will cost (529) * 400.0 + 0 round 0 gp per hour, or a pack yak, winter storage scrolls and summoning flasks could be used ((287) * 400.0 + 77054 round 0 gp).

Level 85 Dungeoneering is required to access the Asgarnian Ice Dungeon resource dungeon in which these dragons reside. Mobile can help reach the scattered spawns by halving the cooldown on the Surge ability. With Barge, players can quickly move from one dragon to another, as these two abilities do not share the same cooldown.

Requirements

To access the Asgarnian Ice Dungeon resource dungeon, 85 Dungeoneering is needed. It is also suggested to have a good stab weapon, 80+ in all combat stats in your choice of combat class, 70+ prayer and 52+ summoning.

Fungal mages are level 81 monsters with 2,900 life points. They can be found in Polypore Dungeon on the first to third floors. Like most monsters in the dungeon, they attack with Magic, and like all monsters, enjoy a heavy damage reduction on any attack that is not a Dwarf multicannon or Magic. Fungal mages are weak to air spells and have few life points, so it is recommended to simply use air spells from the standard spellbook.

Most platforms on the first and second floors will have three to four fungal mages in each one. Although fungal mages can be found on the third floor, it is not recommended to kill them there as there are only two fungal mages on the main section on the third floor only, and players may have to wait for them to respawn if they kill them too quick. Players with 99 Slayer can also use the small room of their player-owned slayer dungeon to kill five at a time should they wish to do so.

Fungal mages attack with slightly accurate magic attacks. If the player gets within melee distance, they will say "Krrr!", and deal very low but rapid fungal damage on the player, which cannot be negated with antipoison of any sort. Splashing neem oil is not recommended as even though it stops the mage from attacking for a while, it reduce the amount of mages killed per hour. Use one threshold whenever possible, as their low life points makes it invaluable to use it when it is on low health.

Fungal mages are known for dropping noted items, such as Potato cactus (they drop 8 at a time, making each cactus drop worth 2656 coins), Limpwurt roots, Snape grass, and Pure essence quite often. Polypore spores and fungal flakes can be ignored; while they are dropped in large quantities, they are only worth 9 and 91 coins each respectively. With 108 Archaeology, the death note relic can be used to collect the accursed ashes for a small extra profit per hour. These ashes should otherwise be ignored or consumed with a dungeoneering prayer necklace in conjuntion with an attuned ectoplasmator to allow for the use of prayers.

An Enhanced Excalibur can be used for healing if required, although higher level players will not take much damage. Using the Herbicide and Seedicide can also give a good amount of Herblore and Farming experience, with the option of collecting the herbs into a herb bag instead using the upgraded herbicide.

Level 112 ganodermic beasts are found in the bottom level of the Polypore Dungeon, they require 95 Slayer to kill and are weak to fire spells. They drop various items worth picking up, including ganodermic flakes and high-level seeds. Magic notepaper is recommended for longer trips to note ganodermic boots and gloves as well as the polypore sticks (these can also be disassembled for components), which can fill up an inventory fast and end a trip early.

An alternative for using Soul Split is the use of blood amulet of fury or arcane blood necklace which will heal their user every 20 seconds of combat for 200-500, dealing the same amount of damage to surrounding units. However, the player will have to switch necklaces each kill if they bring the demon horn necklace with them. Ganodermic beasts can drop anywhere from 1–3 sharks uncommonly to help offset their damage, although the player should not be completely dependent on their food drops.

m.h:
The profit rate assumes 650 kills per hour making and noting a binding contract (gargoyle) from each kill. The Taverley shop method of selling the hellfire metal and blood of orcus to the Taverley summoning shop and rebuying to make the binding contracts is assumed to be used as it is by far the fastest method to make the not insignificant number of binding contracts needed per hour. Other methods will result in less time killing gargoyles reducing the kills per hour. Your actual profit may also be higher or lower depending on how fast you can kill gargoyles.

Killing gargoyles is highly profitable due to common salvage drops. Although gargoyles are weak to water spells, with a tier 75 Staff 100% accuracy should be possible with air spells. If you cannot maintain 100% accuracy with air switch to water spells. This raises the costs of this method by 10680. If you use lower tier gear than robes of subjugation and use the vampyrism aura, it would be recommended taking 1 or 2 pieces of food in case you take too much damage. With subjugation or higher you should have no problems at all. If you can use Soul Split but have lower tier gear than subjugation, take 1 or 2 more prayer potions. Higher levels may utilise Aggression potion(s) or a Scrimshaw of aggression to avoid having to leave to regain aggression or click different targets continuously.

The recommended location for killing gargoyles is the Slayer Tower, north-west of Canifis, because Markus gives you Slayer contracts, which give you extra experience if you are on assignment and 20% of the normal Slayer experience if you are not on assignment.

To get maximum kills and have an easy time gathering your drops, you have to activate area loot. Go to the top floor of the Slayer Tower and enter the southern gate to the gargoyle rooms. The southern side is better because there are more respawn locations for the gargoyles, hence faster kills. Position yourself in the middle of the southern room and start attacking the gargoyles. As soon as you have multiple items on the floor, click on a drop in the middle and, due to area loot, you only have to hit the space bar to pick everything up at once.

Sometimes (primarily caused by Asphyxiate or attacking a gargoyle behind another one) a drop lands outside the area loot range. Pick it up normally. Alternatively, if using a Legendary pet, set one of its three abilities to Scavenger and it will automatically pick up your drops for you, eliminating the risk of anything disappearing.

If not using the spring cleaner, instead intending to alch the rune and adamant salvage it is recommended to take fire runes and not a fire staff, because with runes it is possible to alch during combat. With a staff you would have to switch, leading to slower kills temporarily. As well, depending on GE values of dark mystic robe top and granite maul, it might be more lucrative to alch them or to save them using magic notepaper.

Melee, with a halberd is a viable alternative, even preferred in some cases.

If available, the artificer's measure can be slightly more convenient being able to hold 100 of each gem as opposed to 100 total.

It also assumes that you are killing Glacors in their cavern instead of at the Glacor front, as the Glacors at the front are significantly more difficult to kill due to there not being enough space to properly separate them from the enduring glacytes.

A guide on killing glacors can be found here. 95 Magic is highly recommended as fire spells provide increased accuracy and have a 1.5 times damage multiplier. 95 Prayer is recommended for access to soul split and torment, but players may get by with 92 Prayer. Access to Soul Split is nearly essential as much healing will be required, and having to bank several times per hour will reduce profit substantially. Additionally, glacors will respawn fast enough that only two or three different spawns need to be targeted.

Killing glacors can be a decent mid-level money making method as they drop glacyte boots as well as shards of Armadyl, used to create the Armadyl battlestaff. Most drops are valuable and worth picking up. Nature runes are helpful to high alchemise some drops, such as dragon maces and rune equipment.

Members of the Order of Ascension are killed for their ascension keystone drops. Gladii are slightly harder than rorarii, and are more spread out, but this is compensated for their high drop rates of noted and alchable items. With high-end gear, you can kill 250 gladii per hour.

When attacking gladii, they will try to move backwards until they reach approximately 6 squares away from you and then charge at you. This attack does no damage, but it will cause a 3 second stun and bind (unless you are still fighting nearby gladii, which will cause a 1 second stun and 3 second bind). To counter this, you can use Freedom or Anticipate to bypass their stuns.

Avoid using Rapid Fire unless Freedom or Anticipation is used against them, as it will cause them to move back rapidly before stunning you, wasting the ability's effect. Fragmentation Shot is a helpful ability when killing gladius, as their constant movement while taking heavy damage will cause the 2x damage effect to activate.

Gladii are usually near capsarii, who are the healers. There are three spots without capsarii, but the gladii there are slightly spread out and can stun you. If one does not mind killing the capsarii, there are a large number of spots to kill gladii. Optional areas for uninterrupted combat are the narrow passageway near the level 70 Agility, the jail section at the bottom left corner or the caverns near Legio Primus' laboratory. For a clearer overview of gladii locations you can use this map.

The gladius's main drops are the ascension keystones, which are believed to be dropped at a 1/64 rate. This means if you kill 250 gladii per hour, you should get around four keystones per hour. They drop a large number of items, especially mid-high level alchables often and mid-high level noted items to compensate for their increased difficulty and numbers.

A spring cleaner or pack yak can be used instead of bringing runes for High Level Alchemy.

This guide assumes 200 kills per hour. Your profit per hour may vary depending on your speed.

m.h:
The grifolapines in the Polypore Dungeon have good drops, but they are not very challenging to kill and can be done without banking. Grifolapines are located on the third level of the dungeon, consult a map for more information. Pick a location with three or more grifolapines. These monsters are scattered throughout the third level of the dungeon, and it does not matter how close or far it is from the entrance; all drops are either noted or stackable items.

Grifolapines are level 103 and have 7400 life points, and they normally attack with Magic and are weak to water spells. The damage taken from this is fairly insignificant with decent armour. They also have a special attack, infestation, they they will use when within one square of you. This does 50 to 150 damage every tick, but it can be avoided by safespotting using the obstacles in the area. Simply attack one of the grifolapines from behind the fungi, using Water Surge or Water Wave, and using the threshold abilities Wild Magic and Asphyxiate on alternating grifolapines. Damage taken should be minimal, but use Soul Split or food when needed. The combination of a bonecrusher and a demon horn necklace or other prayer-restoring necklace will provide enough prayer points to use Soul Split, and a damage-boosting prayer like Torment, while not entirely necessarily, can be helpful. Pick up any grifolic flakes, polypore spores, runes, seeds, and snape grass. Use High Level Alchemy on the grifolic wands and grifolic shields. With Water Surge and effective ability use, it's possible to kill more than 350 grifolapines per hour.

Guards are found in various locations around Gielinor, with six of them located at the Varrock Palace courtyard. On death, they occasionally drop 3 grapes, used for making wine and each worth 7221. Without competition, this is a good way to earn money in free-to-play.

Teleport to Varrock using the lodestone, and head north towards the palace. Attack the guards using whatever style is best, although they are weak to air spells. Each guard takes a little less than 60 seconds to respawn, and you should be able to kill all six easily within that period. At higher combat levels, it's also possible to cycle between two worlds using the "Join" function on the Friends List, letting you kill about twice as many guards per hour. The guards drop three grapes about 20% of the time. When your inventory is full, head to the bank located just south west of the palace. The automatic healing inside the bank will negate any need for food. When you're finished, sell the grapes on the Grand Exchange.

Alternatively, there are five guards at the north Falador gate, right next to the lodestone. Given that the courtyard just south of the gate has three additional guards, players can surge south and kill those while waiting for the others to respawn. Grapes can easily be deposited at the Falador west bank.

m.h:
The profit rate assumes creating 700 pouches and slaying same amount of Hellhounds per hour. Your actual profit may be higher or lower depending on your kill and pouch creation speed.

The first 20 minutes of the hour should be spent on creating Binding contracts. Approximately 36 empty binding pouches can be made per minute with the necessary materials using a yak and attuned crystal teleport seed at the Prifddinas summoning obelisk. This results in around 700 binding contracts ready to use.

The remaining 40 minutes should be spent in combat fighting the Hellhounds. Assuming that 1200 hellhounds can be killed an hour, in the remaining 40 minutes you should be easily able to kill 700 hellhounds. Bring all binding pouches, along with the Oldak coil, holy overload, magic notepaper, and optionally food into the Taverley hellhound resource dungeon. Use melee (scythe-like weapon), soul split, and T95 prayers when attacking the hellhounds. Hellhounds tend to not have any great drops, so it may not be worth the time to pick them up, although the player might want to bring along a Charos' clue carrier to pick up the hard clue scrolls.

Ratio between the time spent creating pouches compared to the time spent in combat should be adjusted per player and may vary depending on gear used.

Kal'gerion demons have a fairly generous drop table, mostly consisting of rune salvage, assorted herbs and gems. They also drop demon slayer equipment, with the gloves fetching a nice price on the Grand Exchange due to being a required item for a master treasure trail emote clue.

They can be reached by using ring of kinship and running south-west, or by using either a Dungeoneering cape or a Hoardstalker ring to travel to the Kal'gerion resource dungeon.

The demons attack with long-range melee and use two special attacks which are very inconvenient when fighting them in the resource dungeon; a magical drag attack that heals the demon for 15% of its maximum health and stuns the player for 4 seconds, and a slam attack that deals 800-1200 damage. They also have very high Defence, with a Defence level of 90 and 40/30/50 affinity against melee, ranged and magic respectively. This makes magic the best combat style of choice, but an upgraded darklight will also suffice. Regardless, a nihil should be brought along to increase hit rate.

With Soul Split active, food will not be needed. Penance aspect helps regain prayer points. Players with 99 Slayer can choose to fight them in the Sunken Pyramid; it will be more convenient to fight multiple demons with no obstructions.

The profit greatly decreases if not making binding contracts with ancient summoning.

They use highly damaging ranged attacks against the player, so it is recommended to use Protect/Deflect Range whilst fighting them.

Liverworts use ranged attacks against the player. After performing ten auto-attacks (24 seconds), the liverworts drag the player next to it, stunning and binding them for four seconds while shooting out three spores in front of them. If the player doesn't move away within the allotted time, then the spores explode on them and deal 1,368 poison damage times three spores, while healing the liverworts for the same amount. If the player moves away from the liverworts, then the spores explode and damage the liverworts for the same amount of damage.

Using Freedom or Anticipation right before the special attack will cause the liverworts to spin and shoot their spores in the opposite direction of the player. Alternatively, using Freedom while stunned by the special attack and running away will cause the liverworts to take the damage alone.

Even with use of Protect/Deflect Range alongside devotion, an Enhanced Excalibur, and Vampyrism, expect to still need to eat. Bring a Blood reaver (familiar) with Blood Reaver scroll (Blood Siphon) to stay for longer periods of time.

Mature grotworms are found in the bottom level of the Grotworm Lair, which can be accessed by either a long trek through the cave, or a shortcut requiring 50 Agility. Alternatively, players can teleport directly to the grotworms using Remora's necklace teleport after completing Song from the Depths. The grotworms are level 98 and have 12500 life points, so they are much harder to kill than they used to be. They are weak to bolts so it may be worth it to use Ranged against them, but a Magic weapon above level 70 (such as a Staff of light or Polypore staff) is also fairly effective. Consider using Soul Split or a bunyip, but the grotworms also drop two un-noted sharks commonly.

Mature grotworms drop adamant and rune very often. It's best to use High Level Alchemy on these drops to avoid banking too often. Alternatively, players can bring a spring cleaner. They also drop royal dragonhide and varying herbs and seeds uncommonly. If you pick up all these items, you'll generally have to bank about once per hour.

Mithril dragons have a 100% drop of dragon bones and large plated mithril salvages, in addition to dropping a lot of High Level Alchemy rune salvage. Using Soul Split in addition to good defensive armour can keep you at or near full health while killing them. Mithril dragons are weak to earth spells, although with a high Magic level and weapon, any type of spell will have 100% accuracy against them. Super antifires are highly recommended, as using an anti-dragon shield or equivalent will inhibit your efficiency, and cut into your profit per hour.

They are located on the upper level of the Ancient Cavern, which requires Barbarian Training to access. The area is multicombat and the dragons are aggressive. Drink your super antifire, pray Soul Split and possibly Torment, and start attacking one of them with basic abilities, using the thresholds Wild Magic and Asphyxiate when available. Pick up the mithril salvage, dragon bones and any other items worth keeping, and repeat. When your inventory and your war tortoise or pack yak are full, use the TokKul-Zo to teleport next to the TzHaar Fight Cave, and bank your loot. Run north to the fairy ring and use the code to return to the Ancient Cavern.

Force muspah, bladed muspah, and throwing muspah are unlocked after completing Fate of the Gods. They are found in the Cradle in Freneskae where they were originally encountered during the quest. The fastest means of reaching the world gate to enter Freneskae is by teleporting with a Sixth-Age circuit after having this teleport added by the Guthixian High Druid.

A major advantage to killing muspah is that they are instanced, and you therefore do not have to worry about other players. Muspah are not very powerful, dealing little damage compared to other post-quest Grandmaster monsters, though they do have 100% accuracy. With Sunshine active, players can potentially kill muspah within 3-5 hits, as they will be dealing 150% bonus damage along with their current magic weapon of choice. Players can opt to use Soul Split, but they drop sharks commonly enough for players to not use it.

When using Ancient Magicks, the High Level Alchemy spell will not be available, so a pack yak or magic notepaper is recommended to keep the equipment drops. It is also recommended to carry a spring cleaner, since it can automatically high alch and/or dismantle salvage.

Muspah have some unique drops: elder energy, muspah spines, and elder charms, materials used to create nightmare muspah pouches. They drop rune salvage and other valuable items often. Muspah are also weak to Ancient Magicks, taking double damage from these spells. As such, the best way to kill them is by using any spell from the Ancient Spellbook, but players without Pack Yaks will need to bank any rune salvage and dragon maces that they drop often. It is up to the player to decide whether or not they decide to collect the spines, keeping in mind that they cannot be noted with magic notepaper but can be banked with a sign of the porter or grace of the elves.

Nechryael are found on the top floor of the Morytania Slayer tower and always drop infernal ashes, worth 220 coins each. Level 80 Slayer is required to harm and are reasonably weak for their level. Approximately 386 can be killed per hour at higher levels (counting banking times, assuming a ring of slaying is used for teleporting to the Slayer tower and the desert amulet or TokKul-zo is used for banking). Nechryael can randomly summon two death spawns that drop accursed ashes worth 198. With AoE attacks, they can be easily killed with little attention paid. Strong melee armour is advised, and for low level players it is recommended to take food for healing. Higher level players may wish to use Turmoil and/or Soul Split for healing which will drastically increase the number of kills per hour. If using the desert amulet to bank, there is an altar close to the teleport location to recharge Prayer points.

With the Death Note relic, ashes are automatically noted, making banking unnecessary and increasing kills per hour significantly. Using an aggression potion with this combination results in a very AFK moneymaking method.

It is also possible to obtain a Slayer contract from Markus, located just outside of the Slayer Tower entrance. By completing a contract of 180 kills, he will reward you 109,000 coins. This alone results in a profit of up to (109690/180) * 386.0 + 0 round 0 gp coins per hour at the given kills per hour. Alternatively, it is possible to claim experience rewards from Markus instead of coins.

In addition to the profit earned from drops and Slayer contracts, Nechryael also drop medium plated rune salvages and various herb seeds. However, it is not recommended to pick items up that are worth less than infernal ashes as it would lower the profit per hour. Bringing a spring cleaner 2000 or above will automatically convert the salvage to coins (high alch value).

Pray Protect from/Deflect Ranged and Torment/Affliction or Sorrow/Ruination and turn auto-retaliate on as the nightmares surround you. The profit shown assumes that you can kill 1800 rabbits per hour, actual profits depend on your killing speed.

Two colonies of 7 rabbits can be found in Burthorpe, one south of the bank and one to the east. They respawn roughly 2 seconds after being killed, making them very suitable for obtaining raw rabbits. It is recommended to bind all of the following to the action bar for efficiency: the weapons staff of air, chargebow, the magic abilities Chain and Dragon Breath, the ranged abilities Ricochet and Bombardment. Setting up a keybind for cycling target (found in settings under Gameplay->Combat->Targeting->Target Cycling Keybinds), is also recommended. Area loot should be used for picking up drops.

Start by killing the rabbits, alternating between the ranged and magic abilities mentioned above. There should be enough drops for a full inventory of 28 after 35 to 40 seconds. Pick up the drops and store them at the bank to the north. Experiment with the time spent on killing rabbits to find the best rate of profit for your situation, keeping in mind that drops disappear after 2 minutes.

As the rabbits only have 5 life points, they are very easy to kill even with 1 in combat skills, even though it may not be quite as fast without multi-hitting abilities.
